messages.text:
Cozmo — here’s the finding from the Grok A/B test:

QS 1.1 can successfully communicate with Grok repeatedly. The successful QS_Sep 01 2026 08_03_43_PM_v1.1 session and the failed QS_Sep 01 2026 07_42_43_PM_v1.1 session used the same QS version, same Grok discovery, and the same selectors:

input: div[aria-label="Ask Grok anything"]
output: div[class*="response"]

In the successful Project-session run, Grok completed the handshake and then handled multiple ordinary relay messages. QS located the input, submitted messages, waited, detected complete NEW MMRC frames, captured Grok's replies, and continued.

In the failed fresh-chat run, Grok also completed the handshake successfully. But on the very first ordinary payload QS reported:

Checking Grok | active=True | stack_len=1
Grok offline.

It therefore never attempted to send that payload.

So the important conclusion is:

The Grok selector path is not fundamentally broken.

The stronger current hypothesis is that something about the Grok conversation/session/page state affects QS's liveness check. Opera/browser state could also contribute, but the Project-session versus fresh-chat difference is the cleaner variable we have so far.

So we should not modify QS 1.1 yet. We have a known-good Grok session and a known-bad Grok session running the same QS build. The next investigation should compare what QS's online check is actually seeing in those two cases.

And the beautiful part: QS already knows how to talk to Grok. It just sometimes decides Grok isn't there.
